name: MAX6070AAUT25+T
title: Low-noise precision series voltage references, 1.25 V to 5 V
summary: MAX6070 and MAX6071 are bandgap series references in a 6-pin SOT23 that source or sink up to 10 mA, with separate force and sense output pins. Eight fixed outputs from 1.25 V to 5.0 V come in A grade (±0.04%, 6 ppm/°C max) and B grade (±0.08%, 8 ppm/°C max). The MAX6070 has a FILTER pin for a noise capacitor; the MAX6071 instead has separate ground force and sense pins. An active-high enable shuts the part down; a 2.5 V MAX6071 also comes in a 6-bump WLP.
key_figures: 110 mV typ, 230 mV max at 10 mA (2.5 V)

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit, MAX6070
circuits.description: The filtered version on its own. The supply feeds IN with 0.1 µF to ground, FILTER has its own 0.1 µF to ground, and OUTF and OUTS meet at the output node, which carries 0.1 µF and the load RL to ground. A shutdown control line drives EN.

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit, MAX6071
circuits.description: The version with separate ground force and sense pins. The supply feeds IN with 0.1 µF to ground; OUTF and OUTS meet at the output node with 0.1 µF to ground; the load RL returns to a ground point that GNDS runs to on its own wire, while GNDF goes to ground directly. A shutdown control line drives EN.
notes: GNDS joins ground at the bottom of RL; GNDF goes to ground at the part.

circuits.title: Reference output Kelvin connection (Figure 1)
circuits.description: MAX6070 on a 5 V supply with EN tied to the supply so it is always on. 0.1 µF bypasses IN, 0.1 µF on FILTER lowers wideband noise at the cost of a longer start-up, and 0.1 µF sits on the output. OUTF drives the load and OUTS is joined to it at the load, so drop in the output wire is taken out.

circuits.title: Reference ground Kelvin connection with a 16-bit DAC (Figure 2)
circuits.description: MAX6071 as the reference for a MAX541 16-bit DAC, both on one 5 V supply. EN is tied to the supply. OUTF and OUTS meet at the DAC's REF pin with 0.1 µF there, and GNDS runs on its own wire to the DAC's ground pin, so drops in both the output and the ground wires are taken out. IN and the DAC's VDD each have 0.1 µF to ground; the DAC output drives the load.
notes: GNDS meets ground at the MAX541 GND pin.
The MAX6071 pin marked GND is GNDF.

circuits.title: Precision current source (Figure 3)
circuits.description: MAX6071 on a 5 V supply driving the base of an NPN transistor from OUTF. The emitter returns to ground through R; OUTS and GNDS sit across R, so the part holds VOUT(nominal) across it and the collector sinks ISOURCE = VOUT(nominal) / R.
notes: The MAX6071 pin marked GND is GNDF.

where.VOUT(NOMINAL): nominal reference voltage of the part
where.R: emitter resistor between OUTS and GNDS

operation.text: A 0.1 µF capacitor from FILTER to GND lowers wideband noise and noise coupled from the supply; going above 0.1 µF gains little. On the 2.5 V part it takes the noise density at 1 kHz from 60 nV/√Hz down to 30 nV/√Hz. It also stretches the turn-on time, to 10 ms. Supply noise can reach the output, and an optional capacitor from IN to GND reduces it.

OUTF needs a capacitor of 0.1 µF to 10 µF, placed right at the pin. With switched capacitive loads or fast load steps, a 0.1 µF part in parallel with a bigger load capacitor brings the ESR down; more capacitance and lower ESR both shrink output transients.
About 150 µA, changing by only 1.6 µA per volt of supply.
After a trip across the full operating temperature range, the +25°C output voltage moves by 85 ppm typical.
Typical turn-on with settling to 0.01% of final value takes 30 µs; 0.1 µF on the MAX6070 FILTER pin lengthens it to 10 ms.

OUTF supplies the load current and OUTS is the feedback input, so wiring OUTF to the load and joining OUTS to it where accuracy matters removes the drop in the output wire. The MAX6071 does the same for ground: the load returns to ground, and GNDS goes to ground right beside the load's ground connection.
EN is active high. With EN low the output is switched off and pulled to ground through a resistance of about 200 kΩ, and the quiescent current drops under 1 µA. EN high restores normal operation.
